storyTitle: The house on the hill road
storyDek: A 1928 Colonial Revival that has watched the same maples turn for almost a hundred autumns.
story_body: Chester Hill Road climbs out of Holden Center the old way, following a stone wall rather than a surveyor's line. Number 128 sits where the road levels off, set back behind two sugar maples that were clearly here before the driveway.

Inside, the house keeps its original order: a center hall, a front parlor with a wide fireplace, a dining room that actually fits a table. The kitchen was rebuilt with restraint, keeping the pantry and adding a window over the sink that looks straight into the woods.
Upstairs, four bedrooms open off a square landing. The fourth, over the garage wing, has its own stair down to the mudroom: an office, a guest room or a teenager's kingdom.

storyDek: A 1957 ranch two streets up from Lake Quinsigamond, renovated by someone who liked it the way it was.
story_body: The best thing about 6 Shore Walk is the line of the roof: low, long and unbothered, the way mid-century builders drew houses when they expected the yard to do some of the work.

The renovation kept that. The living room's wall of windows is new glass in the original openings; the kitchen opened toward it rather than swallowing it. Floors are white oak throughout, and the primary suite was carved from the old den without adding a bump-out.
Walk two streets down and you're at the water. Rowers are out early most mornings from spring to fall.

storyDek: An 1840 Greek Revival a short walk from Grafton Common, gable to the street the way the builders intended.
story_body: Greek Revival houses face the street with their gable end, like a temple front made of clapboard. Number 14 does it with unusual confidence: wide corner boards, a full entablature and a door surround that has been painted, by our count, at least nine colors.

The rooms are tall and square. Two parlors connect through a wide opening; the kitchen sits in the ell behind, where it always was. A carriage barn at the back of the lot has been a workshop for decades.
The common is a short walk away. On a weekend in fall, that walk is most of the reason people move here.
